chunks.title: How lasers work & tissue interactions
chunks.tldr: LASER: monochromatic, coherent, collimated → huge irradiance. Gain medium (crystal, diode, gas, dye) in a resonator with mirrors; pumping → population inversion → stimulated emission cascade. Pulses: Q-switching (nanosecond giant pulses), mode-locking (pico/femtosecond). Penetration: UV-C/B → cornea; UV-A → lens; visible + near-IR (380–1400 nm) → retina/RPE/choroid; far IR → cornea/lens. Interactions: photochemical (long, low — CXL, PDT), photothermal (coagulation 10–20 °C rise; vaporisation at 100 °C — PRP, ALT; pigment: melanin broad, Hb blue-green-yellow, xanthophyll blue), selective thermolysis (pulse < thermal relaxation time — SLT, micropulse), photoablation (193 nm excimer breaks bonds — PRK/LASIK), photodisruption (plasma, shock wave, cavitation — Nd:YAG 1064 nm, femtosecond 1053 nm).
chunks.hook: Excimer chops bonds; YAG blows bubbles; argon cooks.

cards.a: Photodisruption — optical breakdown creating plasma, shock wave and cavitation.

cards.q: Why does SLT spare non-pigmented trabecular cells?
cards.a: Nanosecond pulses shorter than the thermal relaxation time give selective photothermolysis of pigmented cells.

chunks.title: Laser safety
chunks.tldr: IEC classes 1–4; nearly all ophthalmic lasers are class 4 (eye and skin injury from direct and diffuse reflections, fire). Laser safety officer, warning signs, locked door/interlocks, cover windows and reflective surfaces, aim away from doors. Slitlamp lasers have built-in filters; others (handheld/indirect, observers) wear goggles rated for that wavelength — optical density is logarithmic (OD 3 = 0.1% transmission; most OD 7).
chunks.hook: Check the goggles' wavelength, not just that they're goggles.

chunks.title: Refractive lasers & femtosecond cataract surgery
chunks.tldr: PRK: excimer on bare stroma — flatten centre (myopia) or periphery (hyperopia); painful days, haze months. LASEK/epi-LASIK: epithelium lifted (alcohol/epikeratome) and replaced — less pain/haze. PTK: erosions, scars, dystrophies, Salzmann, band keratopathy. LASIK: femtosecond/microkeratome flap + excimer; leave ≥250 µm residual stromal bed; no LASIK in forme fruste KC; flap complications (ingrowth, DLK, buttonhole), dry eye. SMILE: femto lenticule removed through small incision — similar results, less dry eye, good for myopic astigmatism. Femto cataract: incisions, arcuate keratotomies, capsulorhexis, nucleus fragmentation — precise and repeatable, no proven visual advantage, costly.

chunks.title: Nd:YAG capsulotomy & vitreolysis
chunks.tldr: Posterior capsulotomy for PCO: Q-switched Nd:YAG, Abraham/Peyman lens, start ~0.8 mJ and titrate; cross, circular or inverted-U pattern; posterior defocus to avoid IOL pitting; apraclonidine 1% for IOP spike; enlarges 20–30% over 3 months. Risks: IOP rise, IOL pits, CME, RD, floaters. Anterior capsulotomy for phimosis: radial cuts, anterior defocus, higher power. Anterior vitreolysis: cut vitreous strands to the wound (peaked pupil, CME, uveitis) with pilocarpine to tighten them.
chunks.hook: Focus behind the capsule to keep the IOL clean.

cards.q: Main complications of Nd:YAG posterior capsulotomy?
cards.a: IOP spike, IOL pitting, CME, retinal detachment, floaters.

chunks.title: Iridotomy, iridoplasty, trabeculoplasty, cyclophotocoagulation
chunks.tldr: YAG PI: pilocarpine + apraclonidine, Abraham lens, iris crypt 10–2 o'clock (lid hides glare); dark irides → argon/FD-YAG pretreat; aqueous gush = patent; ~200 µm; check IOP at 1 h; short steroid. ALPI: ring of large slow burns contracts peripheral iris — plateau iris or when PI impossible. ALT: ~100 burns (50 µm) at pigmented/non-pigmented TM junction; scars TM, PAS, poor repeat. SLT: Q-switched FD-YAG 3 ns, 400 µm spot, ~0.8 mJ titrated below 'champagne bubbles', 180–360°; repeatable; same 12-month effect as ALT. Cyclodiode (TCP): 810 nm transscleral over ciliary body (transillumination), avoid 3 & 9 o'clock; 'pop' = too much; inflammation, hypotony/phthisis; traditionally blind painful eyes, now earlier. ECP: endoscopic, with phaco/vitrectomy, less hypotony. Laser suture lysis after trab (Hoskins lens).

cards.q: Why put a peripheral iridotomy between 10 and 2 o'clock?
cards.a: The upper lid covers it, reducing glare/ghost images.

cards.q: End point for SLT power titration?
cards.a: Just below the energy producing 'champagne' cavitation bubbles.

chunks.title: PRP, macular laser, retinopexy, PDT & macroaneurysm
chunks.tldr: PRP: ablate ischaemic periphery → ↓VEGF. Burns 200–500 µm, 0.5–1 burn apart, 100 ms (20 ms pattern), gentle blanch; sessions of 1000–1500, total ≥2000 (up to 6000+); inferior first (VH settles there); treat macular oedema first; endolaser/indirect if VH or ROP; sector PRP for BRVO. Indications: high-risk PDR, NVI/NVA (ischaemic CRVO), sickle, OIS, ROP. Macular grid: 50–100 µm, 1–2 widths apart, spare 500 µm from fovea; DMO (ETDRS CSME, non-centre), BRVO (VA ≤6/12 after 3 months) — not CRVO; micropulse 577/810 nm (5% duty cycle, subthreshold, confluent). Retinopexy: 2–3 rows confluent burns around horseshoe tears (and selected holes) before SRF accumulates; indirect + indentation for far periphery. PDT: verteporfin + 689 nm, 83 s — PCV, anti-VEGF allergy, CSCR. Macroaneurysm: ring of burns if exudate threatens fovea.
chunks.hook: PRP: start at the bottom, before the blood falls there.

cards.q: Why treat the inferior retina first during PRP?
cards.a: Any subsequent vitreous haemorrhage settles inferiorly and would block later treatment there.

cards.q: Photosensitiser and wavelength used in PDT?
cards.a: Verteporfin activated by 689 nm diode laser (83 seconds).
